Hotels & Resorts Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should

and Investor Relations at The Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts Limited. Thank you, and over to

Abhishek Agarwal: 
Thank you, operator. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the earnings call of Leela Palaces 
Hotels & Resorts Limited for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. We have 
published our quarterly results and investor presentation on the stock exchanges earlier today. 
The same is also available on our Investor Relations website, www.theleela.com/investors. 
 
Before we start, a disclaimer. We would like to inform you that the management may make 
certain comments on this call that one could deem forward-looking statement. Specifically, the 
financial guidance and proforma information that we will provide on the call are management 
estimates based on certain assumptions and have not been subjected to any audit, review, or 
examination procedures. The company does not guarantee these statements and is not obliged to 
update them at any time. Participants are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these forward-
looking statements. 
 
Joining me today are Mr. Anuraag Bhatnagar, Whole-Time Director and CEO; and Mr. Ravi 
Shankar, Head of Asset Management and CFO. I will now hand over the call to Mr. Bhatnagar. 
Over to you, Anuraag. 
Anuraag Bhatnagar: 
Thank you, Abhishek. Good evening everyone, and thank you for joining us. Q2 FY27 was 
another quarter of exceptional performance for The Leela. More importantly, it reinforced what 
we believe is the core of our story. Luxury demand in India is broadening and deepening, supply 
remains constrained, and the value in this market accrues to the brands with the most iconic 
assets and the strongest guest franchise. 
We delivered 30% RevPAR growth, 33% growth in operating revenue, and 36% growth in 
operating EBITDA; a second consecutive quarter of 35% plus EBITDA growth. The momentum 
we built earlier in the year has carried through, while we continue to gain market share and 
sustain industry-leading guest satisfaction. 
For the first half as a whole, operating revenue grew 30% and operating EBITDA grew 38%, 
with margin expanding by 246 basis points. Overall, we have delivered significantly ahead of 
our guidance in H1; and as we enter H2, which is the stronger season for the hospitality sector. 
Rather than walk through the quarter line by line, I would like to focus on what is driving this 
performance, why we believe it is durable and sustainable, and how we are positioning The 
Leela for its next phase of growth? 
The operating environment during the quarter was particularly favorable. Demand was strong 
across corporate travel, leisure, celebrations, and events. Domestic demand continued to

demonstrate robust growth, and international demand also returned in strength. This diversity of 
demand is an important source of resilience for our business. Premiumization was also broad-
based across customer segments, clearly highlighted by higher sales of suites and premium room 
categories, where the suite occupancy rose by over 700 basis points. 
India is increasingly the venue of choice for global summits and marquee events, and that plays 
directly to our strengths. During the BRICS Summit period, The Leela Palace New Delhi 
recorded exceptional operating performance, as our iconic location and premium positioning 
allowed us to capture compression demand at premium rates and further strengthened our market 
leadership. We see India's growing events and MICE calendar as a structural tailwind for rates, 
and we have a strong line-up of events in New Delhi and Bangalore in the second half. 
On pricing power and market leadership, our Net Promoter Score for the first half stood at an 
industry-leading 87, about 13 points ahead of the luxury hospitality average for the Asia-Pacific 
region. This consistency is what sustains guest loyalty, repeat visitation, and our ability to price 
ahead of the market.  
Alongside The Leela's ranking as the world's second-best hotel brand in the Travel + Leisure 
World's Best Awards 2026, three of our palaces; New Delhi, Jaipur, and Chennai were awarded 
MICHELIN Keys for the second consecutive year, with New Delhi and Jaipur each holding two 
MICHELIN Keys. 
 
Our owned domestic hotels, including Coorg, delivered strong RevPAR growth of 30% year-
on-year. This growth was led primarily by a 30% ADR growth to 25,046, with the India headline 
occupancy at 69%, and the same-store occupancy rising to over 70%. 
 
Achieving this on an already elevated base demonstrates the durability of our pricing power. 
The quality of this growth matters as much as its scale. Even excluding Coorg, which was not 
part of our portfolio last year, our hotels delivered a similar RevPAR trajectory. Domestic 
revenue at our owned hotels grew by more than 30%. 
 
Occupancy is also becoming structurally stronger across our city hotels and resorts, with no 
trade-off against ADR growth. Our city hotels reached record occupancy at 74% for the first half 
against 69% last year. Resort occupancy on a same-store basis rose to nearly 60%. Alongside a 
strong weekday corporate base, our city palaces are witnessing increased occupancy over 
weekends, as affluent Indian travelers choose staycations close to home. 
 
Our resorts in parallel are becoming all-season destinations. The Leela Palace Jaipur, for 
example, has traditionally been a winter season property, but it is now drawing strong demand 
through the summer and monsoon months, taking its H1 occupancy well above 60%. 
 
Events are a common thread across both corporate MICE, underpins weekday business in our 
cities, while weddings and social celebrations bring demand to our cities and resorts throughout 
the year. We still have meaningful occupancy headroom across the portfolio, which gives us the 
ability to grow volumes alongside rate.

While the India luxury hospitality market delivered a healthy 13% RevPAR growth over April 
to August 2026, Leela once again outperformed with 17% RevPAR growth. This was driven by 
our superior luxury positioning, strong pricing power, and continued market gains across key 
destinations. 
 
As a result, our RevPAR index expanded to 1.46x from 1.41x, reflecting a RevPAR premium of 
approximately 4,500 over the luxury market. A defining feature of The Leela business model is 
the diversity of our revenue streams. More than half of our revenue, 52% for the first half, comes 
from beyond rooms, spanning F&B, management fees, club revenues, wellness, transport, and 
retail. This adds resilience to our earnings. 
 
F&B continued to deliver with 21% revenue growth, reflecting sustained traction across 
restaurants, bars, banqueting, and experiential dining offerings. We have launched eight F&B 
venues over the past year. 
 
As a case study, Azulian House, our newest F&B outlet delivering a botanical dining experience, 
was launched in May '26. Early performance has exceeded expectations, with more than 90% of 
the covers coming from non-resident guests, which validates our strategy of creating 
differentiated luxury experiences and creating a funnel for the core ecosystem through the non-
room businesses as well. 
 
As our managed properties portfolio continued to ramp up, management fees continued to grow 
and steadily increase the asset-light share of our earnings. Active asset management remains the 
key value-creation lever for us. 
 
Our objective is simple, make every part of our iconic assets work harder for our guests and for 
our shareholders. The Leela Palace Bengaluru illustrates this well. The hotel has been ranked 
number one by RGI index in its peer set over the last four years, delivered a RevPAR CAGR of 
approximately 16% between FY23 and FY26, and is running at a 1.5x RGI index this year. 
 
We converted an idle parking area into the Maharaja Ballroom for MICE, turned unutilized 
space into ZLB23, and launched Azulian House in Q1. Together, these initiatives have unlocked 
new demand segments, strengthened non-room revenues, and enhanced overall asset 
productivity. 
The next wave of value drivers is well underway. Arq By The Leela in New Delhi is operational, 
and the Arq Chennai is scheduled to open this quarter. Development is advancing well on the 
Aujasya wellness facility in Bengaluru, and on renewable energy initiatives in Chennai and 
Coorg. These projects will deepen customer engagement, unlock incremental revenue from our 
existing assets, and lower our fixed costs. 
Our development pipeline remains a significant driver of future growth, and we continue to scout 
for opportunities across both owned and managed assets, both greenfield and brownfield. We 
remain on track for our FY27 openings. The Leela Jaisalmer, a luxury desert resort and spa, and 
The Leela Luxury Residences in Mumbai that marks a new business vertical for us, are both in 
pre-opening phase with teams on board.

At The Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary, our 71-key owned resort rebranded on 8th of July, the 
guest response has been very encouraging, with market-leading ADR, excellent guest 
satisfaction scores, and strong reviews across all digital platforms. We made steady progress 
across all pipeline projects during the quarter. 
Construction continues to advance across Srinagar, Bandhavgarh, Sikkim, Ayodhya, Agra, 
Ranthambore, Tadoba, and BKC Mumbai, and we now have more than 1,000 keys under 
development across marquee destinations. As we continue to expand our portfolio, talent 
development remains a strategic priority. 
We continue to deepen our partnerships with leading global educational and training institutions 
to build a future-ready talent pipeline. The Leela Centre of Excellence has already delivered over 
4,800 man-hours of training and engaged more than 280 participants since launch. We were also 
recognized amongst the Top 100 of India's Best Workplaces for Women 2026 in the large 
category by Great Place to Work. 
To summarize, Q2 FY27 was another quarter of strong execution, and the first half as a whole 
shows that our growth is sustained rather than episodic. Our brand continues to strengthen, our 
development pipeline is progressing well, and several new growth platforms are beginning to 
scale. 
With that, I will hand over to Ravi to discuss the financial performance in greater detail. 
Ravi Shankar: 
Thank you, Anuraag. Good evening, everyone. Let me take you through our financial 
performance for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. In quarter 2 FY27, 
operating revenue increased by 33% year-on-year to INR 4,119 million, with every revenue 
stream growing by more than 20%. 
Room revenue grew 39% to INR 2,041 million, driven by the ADR and occupancy gain and 
contribution from the Coorg. F&B revenue grew 21% to INR1,456 million. Management fees 
grew 76% to INR 289 million, and other operation services revenue, which includes wellness, 
retail, club membership, and transport, grew 25% to INR 333 million. 
Operating EBITDA increased 36% to INR 1,877 million. This translates into an operating 
EBITDA margin of 46%, a 118-basis point improvement over the previous year, supported by 
operating leverage, pricing discipline, and a continued focus on cost efficiency. Profit after tax 
for the quarter increased 27% year-on-year to INR 946 million, supported by a strong operating 
performance across the business. 
In terms of H1 FY27, it was a very strong delivery with operating revenue growing 30%, 
operating EBITDA by 38%. PAT also grew by 72% to INR 1,433 million. We continue to make 
progress in driving direct bookings. For H1 FY27, the contribution to The Leela brand website 
to room revenue rose to 15.1% from 10.5% last year, and from 5.5% 2 years ago. 
This reduces our dependency on the higher cost third-party channels and improved distribution 
economics while enhancing guest engagement. In terms of finance cost, it was broadly stable to 
INR 384 million for the quarter.

For the first half, finance costs fell 37% to INR 777 million, reflecting the debt reduction through 
the IPO. Depreciation increased 24% to INR 336 million on account of the addition of Coorg 
and our investment in value drivers. 
 
Our share of loss from joint ventures is primarily attributable to our 25% stake in the Dubai Palm 
Jumeirah hotel and has improved versus the last quarter. The asset is operating at high occupancy 
through local staycations, though ADRs are lagging given lower international tourism demand. 
We continue to monitor the on-ground situation, and our plans and timeline for the asset have 
not changed. 
 
Tax expense was lower at INR 158 million following the recognition of deferred tax asset for 
Coorg. Pursuant to this, the tax rate for H1 was 16% of the PBT, prior to accounting for the share 
of profit from joint ventures. We anticipate an effective tax rate to be in 20s in FY27. 
 
Our balance sheet remains exceptionally strong and growth-ready. Net debt stood at INR 12,150 
million as of September 2026, and our net debt to LTM EBITDA improved to 1.4x from 1.6x in 
March 2026, and from 3.7x in March 2025, even as we continue to invest in our pipeline assets.  
Our debt has a long-dated maturity profile for more than 10 years, and our AA-stable credit 
rating underscores our financial strength. This gives us ample capacity to pursue attractive 
growth opportunities while maintaining balance sheet discipline.  
Additionally, our borrowing costs have reduced by a further 30 basis points from mid-October, 
as we have actively renegotiated with our lenders, which provides a shield from potential 
transmission of policy rate hikes. 
 
For the Mumbai BKC project, we would like to update that the lease deed in respect of the land 
was executed in September 2026 with MMRDA. To recap, the mixed-use project is planned as 
a 250-key Leela Palace Hotel and a 700k square feet office with Leela and Brookfield owning 
50% share each in the JV. To progress further and get the benefit of an existing government 
scheme, we will now look to buy the entire FSI required for the project. 
 
Since this is a material transaction with a related party, with the JV entity, Leela will shortly 
reach out to the shareholders for an approval of investment. Our long-term plan remains the 
same as it was previously. We intend to eventually divest our stake in our office portion and 
keep our 50% stake in the hotel, subject to regulatory, shareholders, and other approvals. 
 
To summarize, with momentum sustained across the first half, a diversified revenue base, a 
strong balance sheet, and expanding pipeline, we remain confident in our ability to drive 
industry-leading growth. On behalf of the management team, I would like to thank our 
associates, guests, partners, and investors for their continued support. Yes, operator, we can start 
the Q&A session now.
